import pytest

def test_largest_divisor():
    assert largest_divisor(1) == 0  # edge case: no divisors below 1 except 0... range(1) is empty, but 0 % anything
    assert largest_divisor(2) == 1
    assert largest_divisor(3) == 1
    assert largest_divisor(4) == 2
    assert largest_divisor(5) == 1
    assert largest_divisor(6) == 3
    assert largest_divisor(10) == 5
    assert largest_divisor(12) == 6
    assert largest_divisor(15) == 5
    assert largest_divisor(28) == 14
    assert largest_divisor(49) == 7
    assert largest_divisor(100) == 50
    assert largest_divisor(101) == 1  # prime number

    # Verify result always divides n
    for n in range(2, 200):
        d = largest_divisor(n)
        assert n % d == 0
        assert d < n
        # Ensure no larger divisor exists below n
        assert all(n % i != 0 for i in range(d + 1, n))

    # Error cases
    with pytest.raises(ZeroDivisionError):
        largest_divisor(1)  # range(1) yields i=0, causing division by zero
